newsitem.title: USA: Turner plans digital conversion of cable stations.
newsitem.headline: Turner plans digital conversion of cable stations.

text.p: Time Warner Inc. Vice Chairman Ted Turner said Friday he planned to follow the lead of the Home Box Office cable station by converting the Turner cable stations to digital high-definition format "as quickly as we can."
"I think the American people deserve to have high definition television," Turner told an entertainment industry gathering. "We've always had all the latest things and all the best technology."
His pledge came a day after Congress backed off on its deadline for all broadcasters to convert from analog to digital by the year 2006.

Arguing the conversion could leave some viewers in the dark until they had new digital TV sets, the House Commerce Committe ruled broadcasters could keep their analog licenses past 2006 if 5 percent of their audiences were still relying on analog. Earlier in the week, a House panel defeated a provision that would have required all new TV sets to have digital capability by July 1, 2001.
Critics said these delays left broadcasters with little incentive to convert to digital, a technology that offers ultra-sharp pictures and compact-disc quality sound.
But Turner said the rapid conversion of some major cable stations would challenge major networks to act quickly.
"If we convert then ABC, CBS and NBC will convert too because they can't have inferior quality to us," Turner said.
Home Box Office this week broke ranks with a group of major broadcasters seeking a delay in the conversion, by announcing that it would offer digital high-definition programming by next summer.
